title: Brokers and broker contacts backend
objective: Port the broker administration API: tenant-scoped brokers with broker type/tier, and broker contacts with exactly-one-primary discipline, matching the reference contract (P-04 broker admin, section 12 Settings).
scope: Broker endpoints: list (filters/sort/paging), create, get, update, disable per reference API
Broker contacts subresource: list/create/update/remove with one-primary-contact enforcement
Broker type references the tenant broker-type reference list (T-019)
Tenant isolation, permission binding, audit on changes
implementation_details: Mirror .NET Brokers endpoint paths/DTOs; server-side pagination/sorting/filtering params preserved ({items,page,pageSize,total}, default 25).
Primary-contact rule: setting a new primary demotes the previous within the same transaction; deleting the primary requires promotion per reference behavior (verify and port exactly).
Contact fields format-validated (email/phone) with the reference validation codes.
Disabled brokers remain resolvable on historical leads/quotes (N-09).

integration: CRUD + pagination/sort/filter contract; tenant isolation (cross-tenant broker id -> 404)
Primary-contact transitions keep exactly one primary under concurrent-ish sequences
Validation failures return reference codes; audit rows for create/update/disable
e2e: Settings brokers spec adapted in T-043

The task's own npm test / lint / db:validate failures were re-adjudicated on a SERIAL baseline the evaluator reproduced independently: npm test 66 files / 1278 passed / 0 skipped exit 0 (brokers.test.ts among them), typecheck 0 after the full run, lint 0, db:types:check 0, db:validate 0 - confirming those failures were cross-task concurrency artifacts exactly as reported. RULING (unbounded pageSize): PRESERVE AS-IS IS ACCEPTED. Verified first-hand: ListBrokersQueryHandler.cs:15-16 clamps only the lower bounds (page<1->1, pageSize<1->25), and settingsApi.ts:223 calls pageSize=200 for the non-paginating Settings tab, reading totalCount at :209. Capping now would either break a known SPA consumer or require a unilaterally chosen contract change; the read is tenant-scoped so cost is bounded by the tenant's broker count, and the reference behaves identically. The flag stands and MUST reach the AC-095 deviation ledger at T-043/T-044 as an explicit product decision (cap or keep). MEASURED DIVERGENCES ALL CONFIRMED FIRST-HAND AGAINST THE REFERENCE SOURCES: duplicate name is 409 (BrokerEndpoints.cs:130-134) while ReferenceDataEndpoints maps ITS duplicate to 422 - the reference mappers genuinely disagree, so following the local reference file is correct; the broker mapper emits a code extension on every branch (:123-145); the list envelope is totalCount (BrokerDto.cs:33), so the task file's 'total' was wrong and the measured contract rightly won; the list read is membership-only per the 2026-07-13 fix recorded at :29-33. TWO-WAY DUPLICATE MUTATION RE-RUN FIRST-HAND, both proven applied (grep + md5 delta) and both killed: status-only (ConflictError->AppError 422, code intact) 2 failed; code-only (constant value changed, 409 intact) 2 failed - and the code-only kill also proves the tests assert the LITERAL code rather than importing the mutated constant, so the assertions genuinely discriminate on code independently of status. TENANT PREDICATE RE-RUN FIRST-HAND: findBroker forTenant->raw executor (proven semantically: forTenant 0 / await executor 1 in the body, md5 delta) kills exactly the 4 cross-tenant tests the implementor named (detail read, update, disable, add-contact). All restores md5-verified byte-identical. RULING (removal-time promotion): PORT VERBATIM IS CORRECT - RemoveContactCommandHandler.cs:11-20 read first-hand documents that spec FR-24/AC-023 leave removal-time promotion undefined and that lowest-id promotion was the handler's own choice; re-deciding it here would invent product behaviour, and service.ts removeContact remains the single change point. RULING (removed-contact audit shape): before={brokerId,name,wasPrimary} / after={promotedContactId|null} ACCEPTED - the reference's flat details object (:68) had to be mapped onto this repo's mandatory before/after contract; all information is preserved and the choice is documented as decided-without-guidance. RULING (.strict() write schemas): ACCEPTED - consistent with the ratified T-019 precedent, converts silent smuggling of status/isPrimary into a loud 422, both refusals pinned. Exactly-one-primary invariant, demote-before-promote ordering against the partial unique index, idempotent disable/set-primary without duplicate audit rows, and same-transaction audit (strictly stronger than the reference) all verified by reading service.ts against the cited handlers. RESIDUALS: e2e at T-043 (Settings brokers spec); AC-095 ledger entries - pageSize cap decision, unparseable query values 422-vs-400, blank-contact-fields-to-NULL, .strict() bodies.

measured_dotnet_semantics: DUPLICATE NAME IS 409, NOT 422 (BrokerEndpoints.cs:130-134). The sibling ReferenceDataEndpoints.cs:119 and TenantEndpoints map THEIR duplicates to 422. The reference mappers disagree with each other, so this port follows its own reference file rather than a house rule. Pinned by a test asserting BOTH the 409 status AND the BROKER_DUPLICATE_NAME code.
THE BROKER MAPPER DOES EMIT A `code` EXTENSION on every branch (:125-144), alongside detail = "{CODE}: {message}" - unlike tenants/errors.ts, whose reference mapper omitted both. Ported as measured.

The list read is membership-only by a deliberate 2026-07-13 fix (:29-32): the broker picker appears in every leads filter row, the intake form and every dashboard filter bar. The contact-bearing detail read stays behind brokers.view; mutations behind brokers.manage.

List envelope is {items,totalCount,page,pageSize} (BrokerDto.cs:33, and settingsApi.ts:207-212 reads totalCount), NOT the {items,page,pageSize,total} written in this task file. The measured contract wins; renaming would break the Settings tab.
PUT is a full replace: UpdateBrokerCommandHandler.cs:57-59 assigns all three fields unconditionally, so an omitted brokerTypeId/branch CLEARS the column. Pinned by a test.
AddContact isPrimary is a request, not a decision: a first contact is primary regardless (AddContactCommand.cs:6-10); requesting primary later demotes the incumbent.
UpdateContactRequest carries NO isPrimary (BrokerEndpoints.cs:153); the primary marker moves only via set-primary.

set-primary on the already-primary contact returns 200 early WITHOUT an audit row (SetPrimaryContactCommandHandler.cs:41-44). Disable is likewise idempotent without a second audit row (DisableBrokerCommandHandler.cs:27-30). Both pinned.
Removing the primary promotes the LOWEST-ID (oldest) survivor (RemoveContactCommandHandler.cs:58-59).

Broker-type validity requires tenant + id + list_type=broker_type + is_active (ReferenceDataStore.cs:83-92): a disabled type, a wrong-list-type id, and another tenant type all yield BROKER_INVALID_BROKER_TYPE.
The duplicate-name check runs BEFORE the broker-type check, so a duplicate with a bad type reports 409 not 422 (CreateBrokerCommandHandler.cs:40-49).
deviations_from_reference: Write schemas are .strict(): an unknown body key is a 422 rather than being silently ignored by the ASP.NET binder. That is what makes an attempt to smuggle `status` (broker) or `isPrimary` (contact update) loud instead of a silent no-op. Same choice as the T-019 reference-data port. Both refusals are pinned by tests.

Unparseable page/pageSize/brokerTypeId query values are 422 (BROKER_VALIDATION_FAILED) where the ASP.NET binder produced 400. Same reported deviation as reference-data includeDisabled and Tenant Manager includeRemoved.

Blank/whitespace email and phone are stored as NULL rather than verbatim, so a row is never left neither-valid-nor-absent. The reference When(!IsNullOrWhiteSpace) guard already treats them as "no value" for validation.
Each mutation and its audit row share ONE transaction; the reference wrote audit AFTER the store call, so a crash between the two produced an unaudited change. Strictly stronger.
Audit details use lowercase before/after keys per the in-repo contract (audit/types.ts:45-59), not the reference PascalCase.
flagged_for_review: NO UPPER BOUND ON pageSize - ported as-is. ListBrokersQueryHandler.cs:15-16 clamps only the LOWER bound, and settingsApi.listBrokers() relies on pageSize=200 because the Settings tab does not paginate. Capping it would silently truncate that screen, so it is flagged rather than quietly fixed. This is the one place the port knowingly keeps an unbounded read.

REMOVAL-TIME PROMOTION RULE IS AN INHERITED AMBIGUITY. RemoveContactCommandHandler.cs:11-20 states outright that spec FR-24/AC-023 do not say what happens when the primary is removed while other contacts remain, and that promoting the oldest survivor was the handler own choice. Ported verbatim rather than re-decided; a product answer can still change it in one place (service.ts removeContact).

DECIDED WITHOUT EXPLICIT GUIDANCE: the removed-contact audit row records after={promotedContactId} (null when nobody was promoted). The reference put PromotedContactId in a flat details object; the before/after split is this repo contract, so the mapping had to be chosen rather than copied.
